name: Gelatin peel-off mask

card.summary: A gelatin peel-off mask is a home face mask that dries into a film and is peeled away, which users say lifts surface debris and leaves skin looking smoother.
card.note: Peeling a dried film from skin can irritate sensitive skin.

quick.overview:
Gelatin is an animal-collagen ingredient that dissolves in hot water and sets as it cools. Home mask recipes use it to form a film that is peeled off, and users say it pulls away surface oil and debris from pores so skin looks clearer.

No clinical trials on gelatin masks were found. Gelatin itself is a documented cosmetic and food ingredient, and hydrolyzed collagen appears in creams for texture and moisture.
quick.how: Users make the mask at home from gelatin and a liquid, apply it as a layer over the face, let it dry and peel it off. Commercial gelatin mask sheets also exist; a 2010 Korean patent application describes one.
quick.risks: No safety studies on the home mask were found. Peeling a dried film can pull on the skin, and gelatin is an animal-derived product.

lead: A gelatin peel-off mask is a do-it-yourself face mask made with gelatin that sets into a film and is peeled away. People use it hoping to clear surface oil and debris and leave skin looking smoother and pores less visible.[1]

Gelatin is a translucent ingredient made from animal collagen that forms a gel when mixed with water and cooled; it melts below body temperature and is used in food, medicine, photography and cosmetics.[1] Cosmetics often contain hydrolyzed collagen, a non-gelling form, to condition texture and moisturise skin.[1]

A 2010 patent application describes a composition and manufacturing method for gelatin mask sheets, showing the material is used in commercial masks.[2] No clinical trials of the home peel-off mask were found.

chain: Gelatin layer dries on the face
Peeling lifts surface oil and debris
angle.text: Users apply it for a temporary smoother, cleaner-looking surface. The claim of pore clearing rests on user reports.

paras: Gelatin is made by breaking down collagen from by-products such as animal skin and bones and extracting it in hot water. It swells in water, and dissolves in hot water.[1]
A 2010 patent application covers a gelatin mask sheet composition and its manufacturing method.[2]
